implementation_notes: Default realization: a single @Version attribute on the root entity and none on the members, so the provider adds the version to the WHERE clause of the root UPDATE and reports a conflict as OptimisticLockException (or an optimistic-lock failure at flush/commit). One token covers every member change; if you need the token bumped even when the root's own columns did not change, lock it explicitly with EntityManager.lock(root, LockModeType.OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT) or PESSIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT. It replaces per-member version columns and lock rows - choose it while conflicts stay rare and sessions are short.

variants.idiom_name: JPA @Version / LockModeType.OPTIMISTIC_FORCE_INCREMENT on the root entity
pitfalls: Versioning is checked when the root row is updated: if a code path writes only members, no check happens - route member writes through the root or bump the root explicitly.
Retrying after OptimisticLockException requires a fresh EntityManager/persistence context; reusing the managed graph re-sends the stale version.

variants.name: PESSIMISTIC_WRITE root lock with extended lock scope
variants.implementation_notes: Pessimistic realization: find or lock the root with LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE (EntityManager.find/lock, Query.setLockMode or @Lock), which the provider translates into a long-term write lock on the root's database row, and widen it with a jakarta.persistence.lock.scope of PessimisticLockScope.EXTENDED so relationships stored in join tables are locked too. One lock identity for the cluster replaces member locks, and the lock lasts until the transaction ends, so it is the choice when a conflict is expensive.
pitfalls: EXTENDED locks element collections and join-table rows but explicitly not the state of referenced entities, so a root lock alone does not freeze a member that lives in its own table with its own primary key.
Lock scope and lock timeout are hints in portable JPA: behaviour differs per provider and database, so verify the generated SQL (FOR UPDATE OF ...) instead of trusting the annotation.
